newsitem.title: GERMANY: German parliament ratifies Albania airlift mission.
newsitem.headline: German parliament ratifies Albania airlift mission.

text.p: The German parliament on Thursday retrospectively ratified a spectacular rescue operation by German troops to get Germans and other nationals out of Albania last week as the Balkan country slid further into chaos.

German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said in the debate before ratification that since the mission last Friday there were signs the situation in Albania, which he described as "chaos and anarchy rather than civil war", was normalising.

Kinkel reiterated the German government position that sending troops into Albania could not help the situation and welcomed efforts by a European Union team of envoys to help government and rebels find a political solution.
He called on international financial institutions to provide aid to help rebuild the impoverished Balkan country and set it on the path to democracy
"There must be a new beginning through elections set for June and eventually a new constitution. We will not abandon the Albanian people in their efforts towards this," Kinkel said.

During the lightning operation last Friday soldiers opened fire, the first time German troops had done so under hostile conditions since World War Two, breaking a post-war taboo on combat operations outside Germany.
Kinkel told deputies the troops' action had been justified to protect the 116 evacuees from Albanian gunmen who tried to storm five military helicopters that flew them to safety.

"The German army operation was absolutely necessary, constitutional and backed up in international law," Kinkel told parliament, adding that the mission was the only way to get the evacuees out of an "extremely dangerous" situation.

He said that although parliamentary approval was required for such a mission in advance, this had not been possible and that leaders of the main parties in the Bundestag lower house had given their consent instead.
